raw_response:
I am getting old now, so I do not like to take big risks. Twelve mu is not much land, and this land feeds the family, so I still do mostly what has worked before. Wheat and maize go together on most of the land because that way I get two harvests. Cotton I keep on a smaller piece, because cotton can bring cash if the price is decent, but it takes more looking after and more hand work. I cannot read those technical papers, so I look at my own fields and what people in the village do. If wheat looks weak, I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the yield fall badly. Water from the well costs money, so I only irrigate at the important times. I use simple round amounts, not fine calculations.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, using bought local seed or the common seed sold nearby. I put base fertilizer before sowing, then add more around greening or jointing if the crop looks yellow. Wheat needs water, so I will likely irrigate three times if the spring is normal. After wheat harvest in June, I do not waste time because the maize must go in fast. I usually keep the stubble, do quick shallow tillage, and plant maize right away. For maize I do not put too much input, because the season is short and summer rain helps. Cotton I only keep on a small patch. Cotton can earn money, but at my age it is tiring, so I will not expand it. I will feed it enough fertilizer to hold the bolls, irrigate once or twice if it turns dry, and spray only if insects really show up.
